title: VPC route reconciliation race causing intermittent cross-tenant routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple Dedicated tenants reported sporadic cross-tenant connectivity where traffic destined for tenant A briefly reached tenant B's gateways. The behavior appeared during short peering flaps and after rapid peering configuration changes (create/delete) on customer VPCs. Root cause analysis identified a race in the VPC peering reconciliation job: stale routes and stale local DNS cache entries could remain installed for a short window when the peering controller repaired routes, resulting in transient route leaks on the gateway nodes.

Impact: Affected 4 customers (two reported incidents, two observed in internal alerting) with brief windows (10s-3m) of incorrect routing; possible data plane cross-talk for affected flows. Customer-facing outages were short but triggered high-severity escalations for security-conscious customers on Dedicated plans.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create two separate Dedicated tenants with peered VPCs and overlapping route summaries.
2) Apply a rapid sequence of peering create/delete + route updates (simulated by the repro script).
3) Observe the gateway node route table and conntrack entries while reconciliation job runs.
4) DNS lookups for service FQDNs on the gateway show stale IPs until cache invalidation.
Expected: No cross-tenant routes remain installed; actual: short-lived route entries persist and traffic is misrouted.
linked_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/networking/pull/311 - dns: invalidate local resolver cache on peering update
https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4985 - gateway: aggressive conntrack prune on route removal
workaround: Temporary mitigation: set peering changes to staged mode (manual approve) to avoid rapid create/delete loops; restart gateway resolver service on affected nodes to flush DNS cache; apply emergency conntrack flush on the node (runbook step provided). These reduce the window until the permanent fix is deployed.
resolution_summary:
1) Implemented epoch-based reconciliation so each reconciliation run includes an increasing epoch and only applies routes that match current epoch, preventing stale re-applies.
2) Added explicit resolver cache invalidation on peering lifecycle events and a short TTL guard for peered-service records.
3) Hardened gateway conntrack cleanup path to prune entries for routes that were removed during reconciliation.
4) Added e2e tests that simulate rapid peering churn and assert no cross-tenant routes remain. Deployed to canary Dedicated clusters and monitored for 72h before rollout to production.
comments: 2026-02-18 - Marco: Triage complete, reproducer and logs attached. Escalated to P0 due to customer security concerns.
2026-02-20 - SRE: Observed route re-insert on reconcile crashloop; suggested epoch approach to make reconcile idempotent.
2026-02-24 - Dev: Implemented epoch token on reconciliation job; initial unit tests pass. Added DNS invalidation hook. PRs opened.
2026-02-27 - QA: Ran stress test with 1000 peering churn events, no leaks observed after patch; a regression surfaced in conntrack pruning that was fixed in follow-up PR.
2026-03-02 - PM: Communicated fix summary to impacted customers and scheduled postmortem writeup.
postmortem_actions: Update runbook: include forced resolver restart and conntrack flush steps
Add monitoring: detect route-install vs expected state divergence within 30s
Create CI job: simulate peering churn in staging nightly
Document peering lifecycle best-practices for Solutions Engineering
